claims.text: Enhanced oxidation resistance in high-temperature MPEAs is governed by formation of a continuous, adherent oxide scale enriched in Al and/or Cr.
Al and Cr diffuse or segregate to the alloy surface at high temperatures.
Surface-enriched Al and Cr oxidize preferentially to form Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3.
A continuous Al2O3- and/or Cr2O3-rich scale acts as a barrier to oxygen transport.
A continuous Al2O3- and/or Cr2O3-rich scale impedes outward metal-ion diffusion.
Reduced oxygen and metal-ion transport slows subsequent oxidation.
Slower oxidation preserves the material integrity of the MPEA.
Increasing the Al and/or Cr content promotes formation of a protective oxide scale.
A surface-activation heat treatment accelerates Al and/or Cr diffusion to the surface.
Relative to the baseline, the Al/Cr-modified MPEA will exhibit significantly lower oxidation mass gain after exposure at 1000°C for 100 hours in air.
Relative to the baseline, the Al/Cr-modified MPEA will form a thinner oxide layer.
Relative to the baseline, the Al/Cr-modified MPEA will form a more continuous oxide layer.
Relative to the baseline, the Al/Cr-modified MPEA will retain mechanical properties better after oxidation exposure.
The proposed mechanism should operate in air at approximately 900–1100°C, where Al and/or Cr diffusion is sufficient to establish a continuous protective scale.
The proposed mechanism may not apply in reducing atmospheres.
Severe thermal cycling may disrupt scale integrity and invalidate the proposed protection mechanism.
Reactive-element-assisted protective oxide formation is well established in related alloy systems.
